companies.title: Companies
companies.description: The clients apps are built for — companies and natural persons alike.
companies.search: Search by name, trade name or RUT
companies.new_description: A company or a natural person. Contacts and apps are added once it exists.
companies.details_hint: How the client is identified, on paper and in conversation.
companies.empty_description: Add the first company or person you built an app for.

hints.legal_name: The razón social, as it appears on invoices.
hints.trade_name: The name people actually use. Optional.
hints.rut: Dots and dashes are fine; it is checked and stored as 12345678-5.
hints.business_activity: The giro registered with the SII.

companies.apps_empty: No apps for this client yet.
companies.delete_body: “{{name}}” and its links to contacts will be removed. The contacts themselves stay. A client that still has apps, contracts or work log entries cannot be deleted — delete or move them first.
companies.contracts_description: What this client pays for, and the hours of work each cycle includes.
companies.contracts_empty: This client has no contracts yet.

kind.what: Whether the client is a company (legal entity) or a natural person. It changes what the main name is called: legal name or full name.
kind.how: Choose "Company" if it invoices under a legal name and a company RUT; "Natural person" if it is someone hiring in their own name. It can be changed later.

rut.what: The client's Rol Único Tributario, the Chilean tax ID issued by the SII. It is used for invoicing and to tell apart two clients with similar names.
rut.how: Type it with or without dots and with a hyphen before the check digit (which can be K). When you leave the field the check digit is validated and it is stored normalised, without dots. Optional, but two clients cannot share a RUT.

legal_name.what: The company's legal name, the one on its invoices and registered with the SII.
legal_name.how: Copy it exactly as it appears on an invoice, including the company type (SpA, Ltda., S.A.). Required, up to 200 characters. It is the name the panel shows when the client has no trade name.

full_name.what: The name of the natural person hiring, as it appears on their ID card.
full_name.how: Full first and last names. Required, up to 200 characters.

trade_name.what: The name people actually know the client by, if it differs from the legal name.
trade_name.how: Type it the way the client uses it in their branding. When filled in, the panel shows this name first and the legal name in parentheses. Optional, up to 200 characters.

business_activity.what: The giro: the business activity the client is registered under with the SII.
business_activity.how: Copy it from an invoice or the client's tax records. Free text and optional.
business_activity.example: Production and sale of bakery products

address.what: The client's business address: head office or where the work happens.
address.how: Street, number, office and district, on one line. Free text and optional.
address.example: Av. Apoquindo 4500, 12th floor, Las Condes, Santiago

notes.what: What is worth knowing about this client that has no other place: agreements, preferences, context.
notes.how: Free text and optional. It is only shown in this panel; the client never sees it.
notes.example: Pays invoices at 30 days. Maintenance is scheduled with their IT team on Tuesdays.

form_help.what: Records who the apps are built for: a company or a natural person. The client's contacts, apps, contracts and work log all hang from it.
can_do: Save how it is identified: kind, RUT, legal or full name, trade name and business activity.
Note its address and internal notes.
Once created, link contacts with their roles, register apps, create contracts and log work.
Delete it, once it has no apps, contracts or work log entries.
form_help.on_save: Creating it takes you to its page, where the contacts, apps, contracts and work log panels appear. Editing sends only what changed, with the RUT normalised. The client is not told anything and the change is written to the audit log.

search.how: Type part of the legal name, the trade name or the RUT (with or without dots). The service does the matching. Empty shows them all.

company_contacts.title: Contacts
company_contacts.description: The people at this client and what each of them is there for.
company_contacts.no_candidates: No contact matches. Create one first, then link it here.
company_contacts.primary_label: Primary contact — the first person to call. Replaces the current one.
company_contacts.unlink_body: {{name}} will no longer be listed at this client. The contact itself is kept.
company_contacts.empty_description: Link the people you deal with at this client, with their roles.

pick.what: The person you are linking to this client. They must already exist as a contact.
pick.how: Search by name, email or phone and click the person. Those already linked are shown disabled. If they are not there, create them first with "New contact" and come back.
pick.example: Search "gonzalez" and pick María José González

roles.what: What this person is there for at this client. Roles belong to the link, not the person: somebody can be technical at one client and owner at another.
roles.how: Tick every one that applies; you can leave all unticked. Owner decides about the app, Technical sees code, servers and devices, Billing gets invoices and payments, and Approves maintenance authorises maintenance windows.

primary.what: Marks the first person to call at this client. They are listed first, with a star.
primary.how: Turn it on for the go-to person. A client has only one primary contact: marking this person removes the flag from the previous one.

form_help.what: Links a person to this client and says what they do there, or changes the roles of someone already linked.
can_do: Pick an existing contact (only when linking).
Tick their roles at this client.
Make them the primary contact.
form_help.on_save: The link is saved whole every time. Marking them primary removes the flag from the previous primary contact. The person is not notified and the change is written to the audit log.

contacts.title: Contacts
contacts.description: The people at the clients. One person can be linked to several clients, with different roles at each.
contacts.search: Search by name, email or phone
contacts.new_description: Link it to a client afterwards, from the client's page.
contacts.invalid_email: “{{value}}” does not look like an email address.
contacts.invalid_phone: “{{value}}” does not look like a phone number.
contacts.empty_description: Add the people you deal with at your clients.

hints.list: Press Enter or a comma after each one.

contacts.companies_description: Where this person is a contact, and as what. Roles are edited from the client's page.
contacts.companies_empty_description: Open a client and use “Link a contact”.
contacts.delete_body: “{{name}}” will be removed and unlinked from every client.

name.what: The person's name as you know them: first and last name in one field. It is what the contact list and every client you link them to show.
name.how: Type the first name and at least one last name, so they can be told apart from others with the same first name. Up to 200 characters. It is the only required field of a contact.

emails.what: The person's email addresses. There can be several: a work one, a personal one, a team's.
emails.how: Type an address and press Enter or a comma to add it; repeat for the rest. The x on each one removes it. Each address is checked before saving and can be up to 254 characters long. Optional.

phones.what: The phone numbers the person can be reached on: mobile, landline or extension.
phones.how: Type a number and press Enter or a comma to add it. Digits, spaces, parentheses, dots, hyphens and a leading + are accepted, 6 to 20 characters. Including the country code means it can be dialled from anywhere. Optional.

address.what: Where the person works or can be found, in case somebody has to visit or send something.
address.how: Street, number, office and district, on one line. Free text and optional; it is not validated.

notes.what: Whatever is worth remembering about the person that does not fit in the other fields.
notes.how: Free text and optional. It is only shown in this panel: it never reaches the client or their apps.
notes.example: Prefers WhatsApp over email. Not available on Friday afternoons.

form_help.what: Saves a person at your clients and how to reach them. The same person can be linked to several clients, with different roles at each.
can_do: Record their name, emails and phones.
Note an address and internal notes.
See which clients they are linked to and with which roles (roles are edited from the client's page).
Delete the contact, which unlinks it from every client.
form_help.on_save: Creating it takes you to its page, where you can keep editing. Editing sends only what changed. Nothing is sent to the person, and the change is written to the audit log. To link them to a client, open the client and use "Link a contact".

search.how: Type part of a name, an email or a phone. The service does the matching, ignoring case. Empty shows them all.

apps.title: Apps
apps.description: Every app built for a client, with its state and its installations.
apps.new_description: Register an app for a client. Its first key is created with it.
apps.details_hint: What it is, where it runs and what it reports.
apps.empty_description: Register the first app you built for a client.
apps.invalid_domain: Just the hostname, like app.client.cl — no https:// and no path.
apps.invalid_url: Enter a full address starting with https://.
apps.created_description: Created. This is what the client app needs to start reporting.
apps.created_hint: Put the key and the ingest address in the client app's configuration.
apps.created_alert_body: The key is public by design — it ships inside the app — and it is always listed under Settings, where it can be rotated or revoked.

hints.domain: For web apps: the hostname it is served from.
hints.presence: How installations say they are alive. Socket is for kiosks and points of sale: the native app holds a live connection, so commands reach it at once. Websites always ping.
hints.heartbeat: Between {{min}} and {{max}}. An installation counts as connected until {{intervals}} heartbeats are missed.
hints.modules: The heartbeat is always on; these are what the app reports on top of it.
hints.presence_web: Websites always ping: a page cannot hold the live connection, so socket changes nothing for a web app.
hints.log_level: The least severe entry installations send. A device can override it from its own page.
hints.screenshots: Off by default. A screenshot can show the client's own customers, which makes it personal data (ley 21.719): turn it on only where the contract allows it. Each device has to allow them too.

company.what: The client the app was built for. It ties the app to that client's contacts, contracts and work log.
company.how: Pick the client from the list. If it is not there, create it first under Clients. Required.

name.what: What the app is called in this panel, in alerts and in the audit log.
name.how: A short name that tells this app apart from the client's others. Required, up to 120 characters.

kind.what: What the app runs on: a website, a desktop app, an Android app or a kiosk.
kind.how: Pick the matching kind. It changes what is offered: only a kiosk can restart the device with a command, and a web app always reports by ping (it loads the SDK with a script tag shown on the summary).

domain.what: For web apps, the hostname the site is served from. The service compares it with each request's origin.
domain.how: Type only the hostname: no https://, no path and no port. It is stored in lowercase. Leave it empty for apps that are not web apps.

description.what: What the app does and for whom, in a few lines.
description.how: Free text and optional. It helps recall the context months later; it is only shown in this panel.
description.example: Kiosk where the store's customers build and pay for their order without going to the till.

repository.how: A full address starting with https:// (or http://). Optional.

modules.what: What the app reports and what can be done with it on top of the heartbeat, which is always on. Each module adds its tab or panel.
modules.how: Tick only what the client's app implements: metrics and events are ticked by default. A module that is off hides its tab and the service refuses whatever depends on it (commands without "commands", for example). Logs and crashes are kept for 30 days.

log_level.what: The least severe log entry the installations send. Anything less severe is dropped on the device.
log_level.how: Pick a level: debug sends everything, info the usual, warning only warnings and worse, and so on. Each device can have its own level from its page. Installations pick it up on their next heartbeat.
log_level.example: Info in production; Debug while investigating an issue

screenshots.what: The app's switch for taking screenshots of its devices with the "Take a screenshot" command.
screenshots.how: It is off by default. Turn it on only if the client's contract allows it: a screenshot can show the client's own customers and is personal data under Chilean law 21.719. Each device also has its own permission: both are needed.

presence.what: How installations say they are still alive: with a periodic heartbeat (ping) or a live connection (socket).
presence.how: Use ping for most apps. Use socket for kiosks and points of sale whose native app holds a WebSocket: commands reach them at once instead of on the next heartbeat. Websites always use ping, even if you choose socket.

heartbeat.what: How often, in seconds, each installation reports. It decides how quickly the panel knows it is connected and how quickly changes reach it.
heartbeat.how: A whole number between {{min}} and {{max}}. An installation counts as connected until it misses {{intervals}} heartbeats in a row. A short interval shows everything sooner but means more traffic; a minute is usually enough for kiosks and desktop apps. Required.

hours.what: When the client uses the app, per weekday. The usage heatmap outlines it, to show where maintenance fits.
hours.how: Turn it on to set windows per day; it starts with Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 18:00. Add or remove windows per day, and use "Copy to weekdays" to repeat Monday. A day with no windows is closed. Times are 24-hour and a night shift is split over two days. Off means "not defined", which is not the same as closed.

timezone.what: The time zone the schedule's windows are read in.
timezone.how: The IANA zone name, with its capitals and slash. Required while the schedule is on.

form_help_create.what: Registers an app built for a client, so its installations can enrol and report.
can_do: Say which client it belongs to, what it is called and what kind of app it is.
Choose which modules it reports and how often it beats.
Set the client's operating hours.
form_help_create.on_save: The app is created together with its first key (cak_…), and the key and the ingest address are shown so they can be put in the client's app. Presence, log level and screenshots keep their defaults (ping, info and off) and are changed later in Settings. The creation is written to the audit log.

form_help_edit.what: Changes the app's details and how its installations behave.
can_do: Correct the client, name, kind, domain, description or repository.
Turn modules on or off, which shows or hides their tabs.
Set the log level, allow screenshots, choose presence and the heartbeat interval.
Define the operating hours.
form_help_edit.on_save: Only what changed is sent. Installations pick up the changes that affect them (modules, log level, presence, interval) on their next heartbeat. The change is written to the audit log. Keys, updates and CI tokens are saved in their own panels further down.

search.how: Type part of the name; the service does the matching, combined with the other filters. Empty shows them all.

state.what: Shows only the apps in one kill-switch state.
state.how: Pick Active, Grace, Maintenance or Suspended. "Any state" removes the filter.

kind.what: Shows only the apps of one kind.
kind.how: Pick web, desktop, Android or kiosk. "Any kind" removes the filter.

company.how: Pick the client; "Any client" removes the filter.

summary.screenshots_on: Allowed, where each device allows them too

ingest.title: Ingest
ingest.description: The addresses the client app talks to. Only the client apps call them; this panel never does.

sdk.title: Script tag
sdk.description: For web apps: paste this into the page. The integrity hash pins the exact file, so a changed SDK means a new tag.
sdk.unavailable_body: The SDK enrolls with one of the app's keys, and every key is revoked.
sdk.support: With the support module, the app opens a ticket with
sdk.support_more: and reads and continues its own with tickets(), ticket(id) and replyTicket(id, message).

hours.enabled: This client works on a schedule
hours.none: No operating hours. Usage is not compared against a schedule.
hours.copy_weekdays_hint: Use Monday's windows for Tuesday to Friday as well.

problems.order: A window has to end after it starts. Split overnight shifts into two days.

installations.title: Installations
installations.description: Every device this app is installed on. Refreshes every 15 seconds.
installations.search: Search by alias, hostname or device
installations.empty_description: Installations appear here as soon as the client app enrolls with one of this app's keys.
installations.socket_title: Holding the live connection: commands reach it at once.

search.how: Type part of the alias, the hostname or the device ID. Empty shows them all.

connection.what: Separates connected installations from offline ones.
connection.how: Connected means its last heartbeat arrived within the allowed intervals. "Any connection" removes the filter.

review.what: Shows installations still to be reviewed, or those already reviewed.
review.how: Every device that enrols by itself stays to be reviewed until someone confirms it is expected. "Any review state" removes the filter.

status.what: Separates active installations from revoked ones.
status.how: A revoked one can no longer report or enrol again, but its history is kept. "Any status" removes the filter.

usage.daily_description: Online and active time per day, over the last {{days}} days.
usage.daily_totals: {{active}} active and {{online}} online over the last {{days}} days, across every installation.
usage.empty: No usage reported in this period.
usage.heatmap_description: Average active time in each hour of the week, over the last {{days}} days, in {{timezone}}. The quiet cells are where maintenance fits.
usage.heatmap_hint: Point at a cell to read it.

scope.what: Which devices the heatmap is drawn from: all of them or one.
scope.how: Pick an installation to see only its usage, or "Every installation" for the whole app.

status.title: Kill switch
status.description: What every installation of this app is told on its next heartbeat — within about {{interval}} seconds.

explain.grace: Keeps working, but warns that it will stop, and is suspended automatically when the grace period ends. Use it for an overdue payment or a contract ending.
explain.maintenance: Shows a maintenance screen until you set it back.
explain.suspended: Stops working. People using it are locked out.

status.message_hint: {{count}}/{{max}} · in the language the client's users read.

message_placeholder.grace: This service will be suspended soon. Please contact your administrator.
message_placeholder.maintenance: We are doing some maintenance. We will be back shortly.
message_placeholder.suspended: This service is suspended. Please contact your administrator.

status.until_hint: Optional. Shown to the user; nothing changes on its own when it passes.
status.saved: State applied. Installations pick it up on their next heartbeat.
status.suspend_body_one: “{{name}}” will stop working on its {{count}} installation as soon as it next checks in. Anyone using it will be locked out until you lift it.
status.suspend_body_other: “{{name}}” will stop working on all {{count}} installations as soon as each one next checks in. Anyone using it will be locked out until you lift it.
status.until_hint_grace_one: Required, at most {{count}} day ahead. When it passes, the app is suspended automatically.
status.until_hint_grace_other: Required, at most {{count}} days ahead. When it passes, the app is suspended automatically.
status.grace_required: A grace period needs an end date.
status.grace_past: The end of the grace period has to be in the future.

state.what: What every installation of the app is told on its next heartbeat: carry on, warn that it will stop, show maintenance, or stop.
state.how: Active works normally. Grace keeps working with a warning and suspends itself on the date you set (for a late payment). Maintenance shows a maintenance screen until you reactivate it. Suspended stops working and asks for confirmation. A device can have its own state from its page.
state.example: Grace until Friday, for an unpaid invoice

message.what: The text the app shows its users while in grace, maintenance or suspended.
message.how: Write it for the client's users, in their language, saying what is happening and whom to turn to. Optional, up to 500 characters. If empty, the app uses its own text.
message.example: We are updating the system. Back at 3 pm.

until.what: Until when the state is expected to last. It is shown to the user.
until.how: Pick a date and time, in your local time. Optional and informative: nothing changes by itself when it passes; you have to reactivate the app.

until_grace.what: The moment grace ends. When it passes, the service suspends the app automatically.
until_grace.how: Pick a date and time in the future, at most {{days}} days ahead. Required in grace. To give the client more time, come back and move the date.

form_help.what: The kill switch: decides whether the app keeps working on all its installations.
can_do: Put the app in active, grace, maintenance or suspended.
Write the message its users see.
Set until when it lasts; in grace, the date it suspends itself (at most {{days}} days).
form_help.on_save: Each installation gets the state on its next heartbeat (at once if it holds the socket). Suspending asks for confirmation, because it locks out whoever is using the app; reactivating does not. In grace, the service suspends the app by itself when the date passes. The change is written to the audit log.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Only what you change is saved.
settings.danger_description: Deleting an app cannot be undone.
settings.delete_hint: This app has no installations, so it can be deleted.
settings.delete_blocked_one: This app still has {{count}} installation. Revoked ones count too, so the service will refuse while any remain.
settings.delete_blocked_other: This app still has {{count}} installations. Revoked ones count too, so the service will refuse while any remain.
settings.delete_body: “{{name}}”, its keys and its settings will be removed for good.

keys.title: App keys
keys.description: What a client app enrolls with. Public by design: revoking one stops new enrollments only — installations already enrolled keep working.
keys.label: Label
keys.label_hint: Which build or which client this key is for. Optional.
keys.rotated: Key rotated. Update the client app with the new one.
keys.rotate_body: A new key replaces “{{key}}”, which is revoked at once. Builds that still carry the old key cannot enroll new devices; devices already enrolled are not affected.
keys.revoke_body: “{{key}}” will stop enrolling new devices. Devices already enrolled are not affected. This cannot be undone.
keys.none_active_body: No new device can enroll until a key is created.

label.what: A name to recognise the key in the list: which build, installer or branch it is for.
label.how: Free text and optional, up to 80 characters. It does not change what the key can do.

form_help.what: Creates a new key (cak_…) the client's app enrols devices with.
can_do: Give it a label to recognise it.
form_help.on_save: The key appears in the list at once and can always be copied: it is public by design because it ships inside the app. Anyone holding it can enrol a device, and every new device is flagged for review. Revoking it later only stops new enrolments. The creation is written to the audit log.

installation.alias_hint: A name you will recognise, like “Front desk PC”. Empty goes back to the hostname.
installation.controls_hint: For this device only, on top of the app's own state.
installation.channel_hint: Which releases this device is offered.
installation.override_hint: Put this one device in a different state from the rest of the app.
installation.review_body: This installation enrolled on its own. Check that it is a device you expected, then mark it reviewed — or revoke it.
installation.revoke_body: “{{name}}” loses access immediately: its token stops working on the next request, and this device can never enroll again with the same device id. Its history stays. This cannot be undone.
installation.revoked_body: Revoked {{date}} by {{by}}. The device can no longer report or enroll again.
installation.screenshots_hint: Needed on top of the app's own switch. A screenshot can show whoever is using the device.
installation.screenshots_app_off: The app has screenshots off, so this alone does not allow them.

channel.what: Which line of versions this device is offered: stable or beta.
channel.how: Choose Beta only for test devices or clients who accept early versions. Per-channel flags and messages follow this value too.
channel.example: Beta for the office kiosk, Stable for the rest

override.what: A state for this device alone, different from the app's state.
override.how: Leave "Follow the app" so it does what the others do. Pick another state to, say, put a single kiosk in maintenance or suspend a stolen device. Choosing one shows the message field.
override.example: Maintenance, only for the second-floor kiosk

log_level.what: This device's log level, above the app's.
log_level.how: Leave "Follow the app" or pick a more detailed level (debug) to investigate a problem on this device without flooding the whole fleet's logs.
log_level.example: Debug for a week on the failing device

screenshots.how: Turn it on only if whoever uses the device may be captured under the contract. The app's switch in Settings is also needed: without both, the screenshot command is refused.

message.what: The text this device shows while in its own state.
message.how: Write it for whoever uses the device. Optional, up to 500 characters.
message.example: This kiosk is under maintenance. Please use the one by the entrance.

alias.what: A name of your own for this device, easier to recognise than its hostname.
alias.how: Type where it is or what it is used for. Up to 80 characters. Empty goes back to the hostname.

form_help.what: Adjusts this device above the app's settings.
can_do: Choose its update channel.
Give it a state of its own, with its message.
Change its log level.
Allow screenshots on it.
form_help.on_save: Only what changed is sent. The device picks it up on its next heartbeat (at once if it holds the socket). A revoked device cannot be adjusted. The change is written to the audit log.

rename_form_help.what: Gives this device an alias to recognise it in lists.
can_do: Type an alias, or clear it to go back to the hostname.
rename_form_help.on_save: The alias replaces the hostname across the panel. Nothing changes on the device. It is written to the audit log.

snapshot.title: Right now
snapshot.description: From the last heartbeat, {{when}}. Refreshes every 15 seconds.
snapshot.never: This installation has not sent a heartbeat yet.

daily.title: Day by day
daily.description: The last 30 days, today included. CPU and memory read average / p95 / max, in percent.

events.title: Recent events
events.description: What the app reported, newest first.
events.empty_description: Events appear here when the app has the events module on and reports them.

type.what: Shows only one kind of event the app reported.
type.how: Pick session start or end, screen, action or custom; "Every type" removes the filter.

heartbeats.title: Heartbeats
heartbeats.description: Every heartbeat as it arrived, newest first. The charts keep only the last one of each minute; this is the full record.
heartbeats.empty_description: Heartbeats appear here as soon as the device starts reporting.
heartbeats.not_credited: nothing counted online — the previous heartbeat was too long ago

audit.title: Audit log
audit.description: Every change made through this panel, newest first, with who made it. Nothing here can be edited or deleted.

release.rolled_back: Line rolled back to a release

reasons.rollback_rate: The rollback rate crossed the threshold
reasons.crash_rate: The crash rate crossed the threshold

event.what: Shows only one kind of event in the log.
event.how: Type the event's name as it appears in the event column, dots included. Empty shows them all.

resource.what: Shows only the changes to one kind of record: apps, contracts, tickets…
resource.how: Pick a suggestion from the list or type the kind (contract, for example). Empty shows them all.

actor.what: Shows only what one person did.
actor.how: Type their email. The service's automatic changes have no author.

from.how: Pick a day; empty sets no earlier limit.

to.how: Pick a day on or after "From"; empty sets no later limit.

module_off.title: {{modules}}: off for this app
module_off.body: Turn the module on in Settings and the client app starts reporting it on its next heartbeat.

alert_kinds_hint.installation_offline: A device has not sent a heartbeat for longer than the threshold.
alert_kinds_hint.cpu_high: A device's average CPU over the window is above the threshold.
alert_kinds_hint.memory_high: A device's average memory use over the window is above the threshold.
alert_kinds_hint.crash_spike: At least as many crash reports as the threshold within the window.
alert_kinds_hint.error_log_spike: At least as many error and fatal log entries as the threshold within the window.
alert_kinds_hint.enrollment_spike: At least as many new installations as the threshold within the window. A leaked key looks like this.
alert_kinds_hint.release_rollbacks: At least as many update rollbacks as the threshold within the window, across the app's releases.
alert_kinds_hint.contract_expiring: A contract that does not renew itself ends within the threshold's days.
alert_kinds_hint.cycle_hours_low: A contract's running hours cycle has less than the threshold's percent of its available hours left.

json.not_an_object: It has to be a JSON object, between { and }.

hint.channel: The installations on that update channel.

scope.what: Whom it applies to: the whole app, the devices on one update channel, or a single device.
scope.how: Pick the scope; depending on the choice a channel or installation picker appears. It cannot be changed once created.

channel.what: The update channel whose devices are covered.
channel.how: Pick Stable or Beta. It covers every device on that channel at the time. Required with this scope.

installation.how: Pick it from the app's installations. Required with this scope.

logs.title: Logs
logs.empty_description: Entries appear here once the app sends them, at or above its log level.

level.what: Shows the entries from one severity level up.
level.how: Pick the minimum level: "Warning" shows warnings, errors and fatal ones. "Every level" removes the filter. There is only what the devices sent at their log level, kept for 30 days.

search.what: Searches the text of the log messages.
search.how: Type a word or phrase from the message; the service does the matching. Empty shows everything.

installation.how: Pick the installation, revoked ones included; "Every installation" removes the filter.

from.how: Pick a day within the last 30; empty sets no earlier limit.

to.how: Pick a day on or after "From"; empty goes up to now.

commands.title: Commands
commands.description: Collected by the device on its next heartbeat (every {{interval}}), or at once while it holds the live socket.
commands.description_socket: This device holds the live socket, so a command reaches it at once.

types_hint.restart_app: Closes and reopens the app. Whoever is using it loses what they had not saved.
types_hint.restart_device: Reboots the whole machine. Kiosks only.
types_hint.reload_config: Fetches the flags and the configuration again, without restarting.
types_hint.clear_cache: Deletes the app's local cache; it is rebuilt as the app is used.
types_hint.screenshot: Captures the screen once. It appears under Screenshots when it arrives.
types_hint.upload_logs: Sends the device's recent logs now, whatever the log level.
types_hint.check_update: Looks for a newer release on the device's channel.

unavailable.restart_device: Only kiosk apps can restart the device.
unavailable.screenshot: Screenshots are off for this app or this device. Turn them on first.

commands.expires_hint: If the device has not collected it by then.
commands.payload_hint: Optional JSON object handed to the app with the command.
commands.revoked_body: A revoked installation cannot receive commands.
commands.live_hint: Refreshing every 5 seconds while a command is on its way.
commands.empty_description: Commands sent to this device appear here, with what it answered.

type.what: What the device is asked to do: restart the app or the device, reload the configuration, clear the cache, take a screenshot, upload logs or check for updates.
type.how: Pick the command; the line below explains what it does. Options that do not apply are disabled: restarting the device is for kiosks only and a screenshot needs both the app's and the device's permission. Restarting the app loses whatever the user has not saved.

expires.what: How long the command waits for the device to collect it before it expires.
expires.how: Choose between 5 minutes and 7 days; 1 hour by default. A device that is off collects it when it comes back, if it has not expired. For something that only makes sense now, use a short expiry.

payload.what: Extra data the app receives with the command.
payload.how: Open "Add a payload" and type a JSON object, between { and }. Optional: most commands do not need one. Which fields it reads depends on the client's app.

form_help.what: Sends a command from the catalogue to this device.
can_do: Choose the command.
Set how long it waits for the device to collect it.
Add an optional JSON payload.
form_help.on_save: The command waits as pending until the device collects it: on its next heartbeat, or at once if it holds the socket. It ends succeeded, failed, expired or cancelled, and can be cancelled while pending or delivered. The service refuses commands to a revoked device or to an app without the commands module. It is written to the audit log.

status.what: Shows only the commands in one status.
status.how: Pending (waiting for the device), delivered, succeeded, failed, expired or cancelled; "Every status" removes the filter.

screenshots.title: Screenshots
screenshots.description: What the screen showed each time a screenshot was taken. Off by default: a screenshot can show the client's customers.
screenshots.off_app: The app does not allow screenshots. Turn them on in the app's Settings, and only where the client's contract allows it (ley 21.719).
screenshots.off_device: This device does not allow screenshots. Turn them on under Controls, above.
screenshots.off_generic: Screenshots are not allowed on this device right now.
screenshots.empty_description: Send a “Take a screenshot” command and the image appears here.
screenshots.delete_body: The image is removed for good. The command that took it stays in the history.

flags.title: Feature flags
flags.description_panel: Values the app reads while it runs. For each device the most specific one wins: its own installation, then its channel, then the whole app.
flags.key_hint: Lowercase letters, digits, “_”, “.” and “-”, up to 64 characters.
flags.invalid_key: Use lowercase letters, digits, “_”, “.” and “-”, starting with a letter or a digit.
flags.description_hint: What the flag does, for whoever reads this next. Optional.
flags.conflict: This key is already set at that scope. Edit that row instead.
flags.empty_description: Create one, then add overrides for a channel or a single device.
flags.delete_body_app: “{{key}}” stops being set for the whole app. Overrides for channels or devices stay.
flags.delete_body_override: This override of “{{key}}” is removed; the devices it covered fall back to the next value up.

key.what: The name the app reads the flag by. It must match what the code looks up.
key.how: Lowercase letters, digits, "_", "." and "-", starting with a letter or digit, up to 64 characters. Required. It cannot be changed once created; an override uses the same key as the app's flag.

description.what: What the flag does, for whoever reads it later.
description.how: One sentence. Optional, up to 500 characters. The app does not receive it.
description.example: Turns on the new Webpay checkout flow

kind.what: The type of the flag's value: yes/no, text or number.
kind.how: Pick the type the app expects. Changing it resets the value to a default (true, empty or 0).

value.what: The value every device within the flag's scope receives.
value.how: For yes/no pick true or false; for text type anything (it can be empty); for number type a number, with decimals if needed (required for that type).
value.example: true, or 0.15 for a discount rate

form_help.what: Creates a feature flag, adds an override for a channel or a device, or changes one's value.
can_do: Choose the key and describe what it does.
Set the type and value.
Decide whom it applies to: the whole app, a channel or one installation.
form_help.on_save: Devices get the flag on their next heartbeat or with "Reload the configuration". On each device the most specific value wins: its installation, then its channel, then the app. The same key cannot be defined twice at the same scope. The key and scope do not change afterwards; editing changes only the value and description. It is written to the audit log.

config.title: Remote configuration
config.never_saved: Nothing published yet. Installations receive an empty document until the first version is published.
config.document_hint: The JSON object every installation receives.
config.document_required: The document is required. Use {} for an empty one.
config.schema_hint: A JSON Schema the document must satisfy. Emptying it removes it. Supported keywords:
config.note_hint: What changed and why, for the history. Optional.
config.conflict_body: Your edit started from an older version. Loading the latest discards the changes here, so copy them first if you need them.
config.history_description: Every published version, newest first. Restoring one publishes it again as a new version.
config.restore_body: Version {{version}} is published again as the newest version. Nothing is lost: the current one stays in the history.

document.what: The JSON object every installation receives as its remote configuration. The app reads it while running.
document.how: Type a valid JSON object, between { and }; the syntax error shows underneath as you type and "Format" tidies it. Required: use {} for an empty one. If there is a schema, the document must satisfy it.

schema.what: An optional JSON Schema the document must satisfy, so nobody publishes a configuration the app cannot read.
schema.how: Type a JSON Schema object using the supported keywords listed underneath. If it uses others, or the document does not satisfy it, the service refuses the version and lists the issues. Emptying it removes it.

note.what: A note for the history: what changed and why.
note.how: A short sentence. Optional, up to 200 characters. It is shown beside the version in the history.
note.example: Raises the cart limit to 20 at the client's request

form_help.what: Publishes the app's remote configuration: a JSON document installations apply without a new release.
can_do: Edit the document and, optionally, its schema.
Leave a note for the history.
Discard unpublished changes.
form_help.on_save: Publishing creates a new numbered version; earlier ones stay in the history and can be restored. If someone published while you were editing, the service refuses rather than overwrite, and you can load the latest. Installations get the version on their next heartbeat or with the "Reload the configuration" command. It is written to the audit log.

messages.title: In-app messages
messages.description: Banners and dialogs shown inside the app — to everybody, one channel or one device — for as long as you choose.
messages.body_hint: {{count}}/{{max}} · in the language the client's users read.

display_hint.banner: A strip at the top of the app; work carries on.
display_hint.modal: A dialog that has to be dismissed before carrying on.

messages.ends_hint: Empty keeps it until you end it.
messages.ends_before_start: It has to end after it starts.
messages.delete_body: “{{title}}” and its read receipts are removed for good. To stop showing it, end it instead.
messages.receipts_empty: No device has shown it yet.
messages.empty_description: Write one to warn about a maintenance, announce a change or ask the people using the app to do something.

title.what: The message's heading, the first thing the user sees.
title.how: Short and clear, in the language of the client's users. Required, up to 200 characters.

body.what: The full text of the message.
body.how: Explain what is happening, when and what the user has to do. Required, up to 4000 characters.
body.example: On Saturday the 14th between 08:00 and 10:00 the system will be unavailable. Close your orders before then.

severity.what: How important the message is. The app uses it for colour and icon.
severity.how: Info for notices, Warning for something the user should attend to, and Critical for something urgent.

display.what: How the message appears inside the app.
display.how: Banner shows a strip at the top and lets work continue; Dialog interrupts until the user closes it. Use the dialog only for what truly must not go unnoticed.

starts_at.how: Pick a date and time, in your local time. Empty shows it from the moment it is published. A message starting in the future is scheduled.

ends_at.what: Until when the message is shown.
ends_at.how: Pick a date and time after the start. Empty keeps it until you use "End now".

form_help.what: Writes a message the people using the app see inside it: a maintenance notice, a change, a request.
can_do: Write the title and text.
Choose the severity and whether it shows as a banner or a dialog.
Decide whom it goes to: the whole app, a channel or a device (only when creating it).
Schedule when it starts and ends.
form_help.on_save: The devices in scope receive it on their next heartbeat and show it within its dates. Every device that shows it leaves a read receipt, listed under "Seen". Whom it goes to cannot be changed afterwards. Ending it does not delete it, so the receipts are kept. It is written to the audit log.

status.what: Shows only the messages at one stage.
status.how: Active are showing now, Scheduled start later and Ended are past their end date. "Every message" removes the filter.

crashes.title: Crashes
crashes.description: Grouped by signature and version. Reports are kept 30 days.
crashes.empty_description: Crash reports appear here, grouped, when the app sends them.
crashes.status_help: Resolve it once a fix has shipped: if it happens again, it opens itself. Ignore it when it is known and not worth fixing: it stays ignored.
crashes.reports_empty: No reports in the last 30 days.

search.what: Searches crash groups by title or signature.
search.how: Type part of the error message or the signature; the service does the matching.

version.what: Shows only the crashes of one app version.
version.how: Type the exact version as the app reports it. Empty shows them all.

status.what: Shows the groups in one status.
status.how: Open (the default), resolved (reopens if it happens again) or ignored; "Any status" removes the filter.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.description: What the service noticed across every app. Refreshes every 30 seconds.
alerts.empty_description: Open and acknowledged alerts appear here. Rules decide what raises one.
alerts.subject: About
alerts.resolve_body: It leaves the inbox. If the condition still holds at the next evaluation, the service opens it again.
alerts.note_hint: What was done about it. Optional; kept with the alert.

note.what: What was done about the alert, for whoever sees it later.
note.how: One or two sentences. Optional, up to 500 characters. It is kept with the alert.
note.example: The branch router was restarted; the kiosk reported again.

resolve_form_help.what: Marks the alert as resolved, with an optional note.
can_do: Note what was done.
resolve_form_help.on_save: The alert leaves the inbox. If the condition still holds at the next evaluation, the service reopens it and notifies again. It is written to the audit log.

status.what: Shows the alerts in one status.
status.how: "Unresolved" (the default) combines open and acknowledged; you can also pick one status or "Every status". It is kept in the address.

app.how: Pick the app; "Every app" removes the filter. It is kept in the address.

rules.title: Rules
rules.description: What the service watches for. Whoever creates a rule is notified through the site's notification centre: the bell, push and email, per their own preferences.
rules.created: Rule created. You will be notified when it fires.

hints.app: Empty watches every app, including the ones created later.
hints.notify: You will be the one notified, through the site's notification centre. Someone else can take it over with “Notify me”.
hints.app_contracts: Empty watches every contract; with an app, only the contracts covering it.

threshold_hint.error_log_spike: Error and fatal entries within the window.
threshold_hint.release_rollbacks: Rollbacks reported within the window, 1 to 100,000.
threshold_hint.contract_expiring: Days before the contract's last day, 1 to 365.
threshold_hint.cycle_hours_low: Percent of the cycle's available hours left, 0 to 100. At 0 it fires once they run out.

condition.error_log_spike: At least {{threshold}} error log entries in {{window}}
condition.cycle_hours_low: A cycle has less than {{threshold}} of its hours left

rules.notify_me_hint: Make your account the one this rule notifies.
rules.delete_body_one: “{{name}}” and every alert it raised are deleted for good ({{count}} still open). To stop it for a while, silence or disable it instead.
rules.delete_body_other: “{{name}}” and every alert it raised are deleted for good ({{count}} still open). To stop it for a while, silence or disable it instead.
rules.empty_description: Create one to be told when a device goes quiet, runs hot or crashes more than usual.

kind.what: What the rule watches: an offline device, high CPU or memory, spikes of crashes, errors, enrolments or rollbacks, a contract about to end or few hours left in the cycle.
kind.how: Pick the kind; the threshold changes unit and suggested value with it, and some kinds also use a window. It cannot be changed once created: to watch something else, create another rule.

app.what: The app the rule watches, or all of them.
app.how: Pick an app, or leave "Every app" to watch every app, including those created later. For contract kinds, with an app only the contracts covering it are watched. It cannot be changed once created.

threshold.what: The value from which the rule opens an alert. Its unit depends on the kind.
threshold.how: Minutes without reporting (1 to 10,080) for offline; a percentage (1 to 100) for CPU and memory; a count within the window for spikes; days before the end (1 to 365) for contracts; the percentage of hours left (0 to 100) for the cycle. Required.

window.what: The period looked back over to measure the threshold: the CPU or memory average, or how many events there were.
window.how: A whole number of minutes between {{min}} and {{max}}. Required for the kinds that use it. A short window reacts sooner; a long one ignores brief peaks.

name.what: What the rule is called in the list and in notifications.
name.how: A short description of what it watches. Required, up to 120 characters.

enabled.what: Whether the rule is evaluated. A disabled rule opens no alerts.
enabled.how: Leave it on to start watching. Turn it off to pause it without deleting it; to pause it for a set time, use "Silence" in the list.

form_help.what: Creates or tunes an alert rule: what is watched, on which app and from what value you are notified.
can_do: Choose what it watches and on which app (only when creating it).
Set the threshold and, for the kinds that use it, the window.
Name it and turn it on or off.
form_help.on_save: The service evaluates it periodically. When it holds, it opens an alert and notifies whoever created the rule through the site's notification centre (bell, push and email, per their preferences); someone else can take it over with "Notify me". The kind and the app do not change afterwards. It is written to the audit log.

app.what: Shows only the rules watching one app.
app.how: Pick the app; "Every app" removes the filter. A new rule created while it is set starts with that app.

releases.title: Releases
releases.description: The builds CI uploads, signed. They arrive as drafts and are published from here.
releases.empty: No release has been uploaded yet
releases.empty_description: This panel never uploads releases: CI does, signing each build with the app's private key. Each one arrives as a draft and nobody is offered it until you publish it.
releases.setup_incomplete_title: Uploads are not fully set up
releases.setup_no_key: This app has no release public key, so the service will refuse every upload.
releases.setup_no_token: This app has no active CI token, so nothing can upload a release.

help.title: How CI uploads a release
help.key_title: 1. Generate the Ed25519 key pair and save the public half on the app
help.key_body: The private key stays a CI secret and the public one is pasted in Settings. The same public key ships inside the app, so its updater can verify what it downloads.
help.token_body: It is shown once. Store it as a CI secret (for instance CUSTOM_APPS_CI_TOKEN).
help.upload_body: The signature is Ed25519 over the raw SHA-256 digest of the file, in base64. The body is the file itself, up to {{max}}. Replace version, platform, architecture and filename with each build's.
help.upload_after: It arrives as a draft. Publish it from its page, starting with a small percentage.

channel.how: Pick Stable or Beta; "Any channel" removes the filter.

platform.what: Shows only the releases for one system.
platform.how: Pick Windows, macOS, Linux, Android or Web; "Any platform" removes the filter.

arch.what: Shows only the releases for one processor architecture.
arch.how: Pick the architecture (x86_64, aarch64…); "Any architecture" removes the filter.

status.what: Shows only the releases in one status.
status.how: Draft (uploaded by CI, not published yet), published, paused or withdrawn; "Any status" removes the filter.

release.title: Version {{version}}
release.download_failed: The artifact could not be downloaded.
release.publish_body: Choose how much of the line gets it. Devices are bucketed by a fixed number, so the ones inside 10 % of this release are the ones inside 10 % of the next: always the same canaries. Start small and widen it once the first devices report healthy.
release.rollout_body: Widening it offers it to more of the line. Narrowing it stops offering it outside the new reach, but uninstalls it nowhere.
release.named_hint: Offered it whatever the percentage says: the canary kiosks. The list shows the active devices on the release's channel and platform.
release.named_empty: No active device is on this release's channel and platform.
release.nobody_body: At 0 % and with no named devices it is published but offered to no device until you widen the rollout.
release.pause_body: It stops being offered to new devices. Devices that installed it keep it. You can resume it later at the same rollout.
release.resume_warning: Resumed without fixing the cause, the service pauses it again at the next evaluation.
release.withdraw_body: Nobody else is offered it, and every device running it is offered the newest earlier version of its line as a mandatory rollback. A withdrawn release cannot be published again; going back to it means rolling the line back.
release.rollback: Roll the line back to this
release.rollback_title: Roll the line back to version {{version}}?
release.rollback_body: Every published or paused release newer than {{version}} on the {{line}} line is withdrawn, and this one is published to 100 % of the line. Devices on a newer version are offered {{version}} as a mandatory rollback on their next heartbeat (at once, holding a socket).
release.delete_body: Version {{version}} and its file “{{filename}}” are deleted for good. Getting it back means CI uploading it again.
release.reason_hint: Optional. Kept on the release and in the audit log.

done.withdraw: Release withdrawn. Devices running it will be offered a rollback.
done.rollback: Line rolled back. Devices on newer versions will be offered this one as a rollback.

release.draft_body: Nobody is offered this release yet. Check the file and the notes, and publish it at a small percentage.
release.reach_description: Who is offered it, and how many devices on the line already run it.
release.reach_published: of the line is offered it
release.reach_stopped: of the line, but not offered
release.notes_hint: What changed. The updater can show them before installing.
release.min_version_hint: Optional. Devices below it must update before they carry on. It cannot be above {{version}}.
release.min_version_invalid: It has to be a semantic version, e.g. 1.4.0.
release.min_version_value: Devices below {{min}} must update before they carry on: for them it is mandatory.
release.min_version_none: No minimum version: the update is optional for everybody.
release.signature_hint: The service verified the signature against the app's public key before it stored the release. Devices verify it again over what they download.

stats.health_ok_detail: Started, reached the API and passed their own checks.
stats.rolled_back_detail: Went back to the previous version on their own.
stats.failed_detail: Could not download or install it.
stats.crashed_detail: Reported a crash on this version since it was published.

status_reason.auto_rollback_rate_one: The rollback rate reached {{rate}}, past the {{threshold}} threshold, with {{sample}} device behind it.
status_reason.auto_rollback_rate_other: The rollback rate reached {{rate}}, past the {{threshold}} threshold, with {{sample}} devices behind it.
status_reason.auto_crash_rate_one: The crash rate reached {{rate}}, past the {{threshold}} threshold, with {{sample}} device behind it.
status_reason.auto_crash_rate_other: The crash rate reached {{rate}}, past the {{threshold}} threshold, with {{sample}} devices behind it.
status_reason.auto_after: Nobody new is offered it; devices that installed it keep it. Fix the cause and publish a new version, withdraw it, or resume it if it was a false alarm.
status_reason.paused_body: Nobody new is offered it; devices that installed it keep it.
status_reason.withdrawn_body: Nobody is offered it, and devices running it are offered the previous version of their line as a mandatory rollback.
status_reason.withdrawn_by_rollback: Withdrawn when the line was rolled back to version {{version}}. Devices running it are offered that version as a mandatory rollback.
status_reason.rolled_back_title: Line rolled back to this version by {{by}} on {{date}}
status_reason.rolled_back_body: It was published to 100 % of the line and the newer releases were withdrawn.

percent.what: Which share of the line (app, channel, platform and architecture) gets the release.
percent.how: Move the slider, type a number from 0 to 100 or use the shortcuts. Devices are split by a fixed number, so the first 10 % are always the same ones. Start small and widen it once the first ones report healthy. With 0 % and no named devices it is offered to nobody.

named.what: Devices offered the release whatever the percentage: the canaries.
named.how: Tick the test devices (the office kiosk, for example). The active devices on the release's channel and platform are listed. Optional.

reason.what: Why this action is taken, for whoever reads the release later.
reason.how: One concrete sentence. Optional, up to 500 characters. It is kept on the release and in the audit log.
reason.example: The printer driver fails on the Lo Barnechea kiosks

notes.what: What changed in this version. The app's updater can show it before installing.
notes.how: Free text, one line per change, in the users' language. Optional, up to 10,000 characters.
notes.example:
- Fixes receipt printing
- Faster payment screen

min_version.what: The minimum version: devices on a lower version must update before they can keep using the app.
min_version.how: A semantic version (major.minor.patch) no higher than this release. Empty forces nobody. Use it for versions with a serious problem or incompatible with the server.

edit_form_help.what: Edits this release's notes and minimum version.
can_do: Write or correct the release notes.
Set or clear the minimum version.
edit_form_help.on_save: Only what changed is sent. With a minimum version, devices below it get the offer as mandatory on their next heartbeat. The file and the signature do not change. It is written to the audit log.

form_help_publish.what: Publishes this draft and chooses which devices on its line are offered it.
can_do: Choose the share of the line.
Name canary devices that always get it.
form_help_publish.on_save: The release becomes published. Devices in reach see it offered on their next heartbeat (at once if they hold the socket), download it, verify it against the public key and report each step. If the rollback or crash rates pass the app's thresholds, the rollout pauses itself. It is written to the audit log.

form_help_rollout.what: Changes how many devices on the line are offered this release.
can_do: Widen or narrow the percentage.
Add or remove named devices.
form_help_rollout.on_save: Widening it offers it to more devices on their next heartbeat. Narrowing it stops offering it outside the new reach, but uninstalls it from no device. It is written to the audit log.

can_do: Note why it is paused.
form_help_pause.on_save: It stops being offered to new devices; those that installed it keep it. It can be resumed later with the same rollout. The reason is kept on the release and in the audit log.

form_help_withdraw.what: Withdraws this release from its line.
can_do: Note why it is withdrawn.
form_help_withdraw.on_save: Nobody else gets it, and every device running it is offered the newest earlier version of its line as a mandatory rollback. A withdrawn release cannot be published again. The reason is kept on the release and in the audit log.

form_help_rollback.what: Rolls the line back to this release.
can_do: Note why the line is rolled back.
form_help_rollback.on_save: Every newer published or paused release on the line is withdrawn and this one is published at 100 %. Devices on a newer version get it as a mandatory rollback on their next heartbeat. The reason is kept on the release and in the audit log.

release_settings.title: Updates
release_settings.description: The key every upload is verified against, and the numbers a rollout is run by.
release_settings.no_key_body: The service refuses every CI upload until you save one.
release_settings.key_hint: The raw 32 bytes of the Ed25519 public key, in base64 (44 characters). Empty removes it.
release_settings.key_invalid: Not an Ed25519 public key: it has to be 32 bytes in base64, not a PEM or hex.
release_settings.key_how: How to generate the key pair
release_settings.key_how_body: Do it once, wherever the private key will live. The private key stays a CI secret; the public one is pasted here and ships inside the app.
release_settings.health_timeout_hint: {{duration}} for the new version to report healthy before the device goes back.
release_settings.max_failures_hint: How many times a device tries the same release before it stops trying.
release_settings.pause_rollback_hint: Of the devices that finished updating, the share that went back.
release_settings.pause_crash_hint: Of the devices that installed it, the share that reported a crash on it.
release_settings.pause_sample: A rate needs at least three devices behind it before it pauses a rollout: one kiosk out of two is not a trend.
release_settings.replace_body: Builds already installed verify downloads with the old key, so they will refuse every release signed with the new one. Change the key only once a build carrying the new one is out.
release_settings.clear_body: The service will refuse every CI upload until you save another. Releases already uploaded do not change.

key.what: The Ed25519 public key every build CI uploads is verified against. The same key ships inside the app, so its updater can verify what it downloads.
key.how: Paste the raw 32 bytes of the public key in base64: 44 characters, usually ending in "=" (base64url is accepted too). A PEM or hex will not do. Empty removes it, and with no key the service refuses every upload. Replacing it asks for confirmation: do it only once a build carrying the new one is already out.

health_timeout.what: How long a device waits for the new version to report healthy before going back to the previous one.
health_timeout.how: A whole number of seconds between 30 and 86,400 (24 hours); 600 (10 minutes) by default. Raise it if the app is slow to start. Required.

max_failures.what: How many times a device tries to install the same release before giving up.
max_failures.how: A whole number between 1 and 100; 3 by default. Required.

pause_rollback.what: The rollback rate at which a rollout pauses itself.
pause_rollback.how: A whole number from 1 to 100; 20 by default. It is measured over the devices that finished updating and needs at least three devices behind it to pause. Required.
pause_rollback.example: 20 (if 2 of 10 devices roll back, it pauses)

pause_crash.what: The share of devices crashing on the new version at which a rollout pauses itself.
pause_crash.how: A whole number from 1 to 100; 20 by default. It is measured over the devices that installed it and needs at least three devices behind it. Required.

form_help.what: Configures the app's updater: the key releases are verified with and the numbers every rollout runs by.
can_do: Save, replace or remove the release public key.
Set each device's health timeout and failed attempts.
Set the rollback and crash rates that pause a rollout.
form_help.on_save: Only what changed is sent. Replacing or removing the key asks for confirmation, because installed builds verify with the old one. The numbers apply to rollouts from now on. The change is written to the audit log.

ci_tokens.title: CI tokens
ci_tokens.description: What CI uploads this app's releases with. They are secrets: a token is shown once and only its beginning afterwards. Revoking one stops the next upload; the releases it already uploaded do not change.
ci_tokens.label: Label
ci_tokens.label_hint: Which repository or workflow uses it. Optional.
ci_tokens.once_body: This is the only time it is shown. The service keeps only its hash: if you lose it, revoke it and create another.
ci_tokens.created_hint: Store it as a CI secret and upload with “Authorization: Bearer <token>”.
ci_tokens.revoke_body: “{{token}}” will no longer be able to upload releases. The releases it already uploaded do not change. This cannot be undone.
ci_tokens.empty: This app has no CI tokens
ci_tokens.empty_description: Create one so CI can upload releases.

label.what: A name to recognise the token: which repository or CI workflow uses it.
label.how: Free text and optional, up to 120 characters. Only the token's prefix is shown afterwards, so the label is what identifies it.

form_help.what: Creates a secret token (cic_…) CI uploads releases to this app with.
can_do: Give it a label to know where it is used.
form_help.on_save: The token is shown only once, in the next dialog: copy it into a CI secret. The service keeps only its hash, so if it is lost it has to be revoked and replaced. The creation is written to the audit log.

update_reports.title: Update reports
update_reports.description: Every step devices reported, newest first.
update_reports.empty: No device has reported anything yet
update_reports.empty_description: Devices report when they download, install, come up healthy, roll back or fail.

installation_updates.title: Updates
installation_updates.description: What this device would be offered right now, and every step it reported.
installation_updates.rollback_hint: The version it runs was withdrawn, so it is being sent back to an earlier one. It is mandatory.
installation_updates.mandatory_hint: It runs a version below the minimum ({{min}}), so it has to update before it carries on.
installation_updates.health_value_other: {{duration}} to report healthy · up to {{count}} attempts
installation_updates.no_offer: Nothing is offered: it runs {{version}} and its line has no newer release that reaches it, or the app is in grace or suspended.
installation_updates.reports_empty: This device has not reported any update.

grace_allowances_hint.updates: During grace the apps keep receiving updates.
grace_allowances_hint.support: During grace the app can still open and continue support tickets.

contracts.title: Contracts
contracts.description: What each client pays for, which apps it covers and how many hours of work each cycle includes. The ones ending first come first.
contracts.empty_description: Create the first one to track a client's included hours, renewal and grace period.

status.what: Shows only the contracts in one status.
status.how: Pick a status: scheduled (not started yet), active, in grace (ended, grace days running), ended or cancelled. "Every status" removes the filter. It is kept in the address, so it can be shared.

company.how: Pick the client from the list; "Every client" removes the filter. It is kept in the address.

contract.renew_body: It covers up to {{date}} today. Pick its new last day: later than the current one and no earlier than today.
contract.renew_body_open: Pick its new last day, or leave it open-ended.
contract.renew_lapsed_body: Renewing it brings the apps its lapse put in grace or suspended back to active.
contract.renew_too_early: It has to be {{date}} or later.
contract.cancel_body: From today no new cycles start and nothing more is sent about this contract. The running cycle closes at its normal end. The apps are left as they are — use each app's kill switch to suspend them. This cannot be undone.
contract.cancel_reason_hint: Optional. It is kept in the audit log.
contract.cancelled_body: Cancelled on {{date}} by {{by}}. It can no longer be edited or renewed — create a new contract to carry on.
contract.grace_body: The contract ended without renewal and its apps are in grace until {{date}}; they are suspended after that. Renewing it reactivates them.
contract.grace_body_short: The contract ended without renewal and its apps are in grace. Renewing it reactivates them.
contract.ended_body: It ended and its grace period is over. Renewing it reactivates the apps its lapse suspended.
contract.expiring_notified: The client was notified on {{date}}, and the covered apps show the end-of-contract notice.
contract.expiring_body: It does not renew itself. The client is notified within the notice period.
contract.rollover_on: Unused hours carry into the next cycle
contract.rollover_off: Unused hours are lost when the cycle closes
contract.no_grace: No grace: the apps are suspended when it lapses
contract.apps_none: This contract covers no app: its hours are for the client as a whole.
contract.lifecycle_hint: What the service did with this contract on its own, and who changed it.
contract.history_description: Every change to this contract and its cycles, newest first.
contract.delete_body: “{{name}}” will be deleted for good. Only a contract with no closed cycles and no logged work can be deleted; otherwise, cancel it.
contract.delete_refused: This contract has closed cycles or logged work, so it is history: cancel it instead of deleting it.

renew_until.what: The contract's new last day covered, inclusive.
renew_until.how: Pick a day after the current last day and no earlier than today, or use the month shortcuts. Required unless you tick "No end date".

renew_open_ended.what: Renews the contract with no end date: it becomes open-ended.
renew_open_ended.how: Turn it on when the agreement runs until someone cancels it. An open-ended contract never ends or sends end-of-contract notices.

cancel_reason.what: Why the contract is being cancelled, for whoever reads the history later.
cancel_reason.how: One or two sentences. Optional, up to 500 characters. It is kept in the audit log and the contract's history; the client does not see it.
cancel_reason.example: The client switched providers as of April.

renew_form_help.what: Extends the contract's term to a new last day, or makes it open-ended.
can_do: Pick the new last day, by hand or with the month shortcuts.
Leave it with no end date.
renew_form_help.on_save: The contract stays active until the new date. If it had already ended, the apps its lapse put in grace or suspended become active again. Hour cycles continue where they were. The renewal is written to the audit log.

cancel_form_help.what: Cancels the contract as of today, with an optional reason.
can_do: Note why it is being cancelled.
cancel_form_help.on_save: From today no new cycles start and no more notices are sent; the running cycle closes on its normal date. The apps stay as they are: to suspend them, use each app's kill switch. The cancellation is written to the audit log and cannot be undone: a cancelled contract cannot be edited or renewed.

contract_editor.description: Hours are typed in hours and stored as exact minutes.
contract_editor.term_hint: Dates are calendar days in the service's time zone.
contract_editor.hours_hint: How many hours of work each cycle includes, what going over costs and what happens to the unused ones.
contract_editor.grace_hint: What happens to the apps when the contract lapses without renewal.
contract_editor.apps_hint: An app may be covered by successive contracts, but never by two in the same dates.
contract_editor.apps_empty: This client has no apps yet. The contract can be created anyway — its hours will be for the client as a whole.

hints.name: As you would name it on an invoice, e.g. “Maintenance 2026”.
hints.company_fixed: The client does not change once the contract exists.
hints.anchored: A cycle already exists: cycles are computed from this value, so it cannot change.
hints.ends_on: Inclusive. Empty leaves the contract open-ended.
hints.auto_renew: When it reaches its last day it extends itself; it never lapses and the client is not notified.
hints.auto_renew_no_end: With no last day there is nothing to renew — an open-ended contract already carries on.
hints.notice_days: How many days before the end the client is notified and the apps show the notice. 0 to {{max}}.
hints.cycle_period: Cycles start on the contract's first day.
hints.included_hours: Decimals work: 12.5 is 12 h 30 min. 0 when everything is billed by the hour.
hints.overage_rate: What each hour over the cycle's available hours costs.
hints.rollover: Whatever a cycle does not use is added to the next, within the limits below.
hints.rollover_max_cycles: How many cycles carried hours survive. Empty, no limit.
hints.grace_days: 0 to {{max}}. At 0 the apps are suspended as soon as it lapses.
hints.grace_message: What the apps show while in grace. Optional.
hints.notes: For this panel only; the client never sees them.

errors.money_clp: An amount in pesos, with no decimals.
errors.money_uf: An amount in UF, with up to two decimals.
errors.ends_before: It cannot be before the first day.
errors.hours: A number of hours, 0 or more.
errors.anchored: The first day and the cycle length can no longer change: at least one cycle exists, and cycles are computed from them.
errors.app_clash: One of the apps is already covered by another contract in those dates. ({{detail}})
errors.cancelled: A cancelled contract cannot be edited or renewed. Create a new one.
errors.ends_before_cycle: A cycle already starts after that last day.
errors.foreign_app: Every app has to belong to the contract's client.

contract_editor.scope_hint: Who is billed, what the contract is called and which apps it covers.
contract_editor.price_hint: How much is charged, and how often.

company.what: The client paying for this contract. It decides which apps can be covered.
company.how: Pick it from the list. Changing it unticks the covered apps, because they belonged to the previous client. Required when creating; it cannot be changed afterwards: for another client, create another contract.

name.what: What the contract is called in the panel, in notices and in alerts.
name.how: Use the name you would put on the invoice, with the year if it renews by periods. Required, up to 160 characters.

apps.what: The client's apps the contract applies to: its hours, its end-of-contract notice and its grace period.
apps.how: Pick the client first; its apps appear. Tick the ones it covers. You may tick none: the hours are then for the client as a whole. An app cannot be in two contracts with overlapping dates; the service refuses it and names the app.

starts_on.what: The first day covered. Hour cycles are counted from this day.
starts_on.how: Pick a calendar day (read in the service's time zone, America/Santiago). Required. Once a cycle exists it cannot be changed: cycles are computed from it.

ends_on.what: The last day covered, inclusive. Notice days and grace are counted from it.
ends_on.how: Pick a day on or after the first one. Leave it empty for an open-ended contract, which never ends or sends notices.

auto_renew.what: Whether the contract extends itself when it reaches its last day, by the months you set.
auto_renew.how: Turn it on for contracts that continue until someone says otherwise. A self-renewing contract never ends, so no end-of-contract notice is sent to the client. With no last day it does nothing: an open-ended contract already continues.

renewal_months.what: How many months the contract is extended each time it renews itself.
renewal_months.how: A whole number between 1 and 120. Required while "Renews itself" is on.

notice_days.what: How many days before the last day the end of the contract is announced.
notice_days.how: A whole number from 0 to {{max}}. On that day the service emails the client and the covered apps show the notice; the panel flags the contract as "ending soon". With 0 there is no notice. It does not apply when the contract renews itself.

amount.what: What the contract charges each billing period, and the currency.
amount.how: Type the amount and pick the currency beside it. CLP takes whole pesos, no decimals; UF takes up to two decimals. Required: use 0 when no fixed amount is charged. Changing the currency also re-reads the overage rate.
amount.example: 450000 CLP a month, or 12.5 UF a month

billing_period.what: How often the amount is charged: monthly, yearly or once.
billing_period.how: Pick the period agreed with the client. It is shown beside the amount and does not have to match the length of the hour cycle: a yearly contract can have monthly cycles.

cycle_period.what: The length of each hour cycle: daily, weekly or monthly. The included hours renew every cycle.
cycle_period.how: Pick the agreement's period. Cycles start on the contract's first day. Once a cycle exists it cannot be changed.
cycle_period.example: Monthly: from the 1st to the last day of each month, if the contract starts on a 1st

included_hours.what: The hours of work each cycle includes, which the work log is counted against.
included_hours.how: A number of hours, 0 or more; decimals are fine (12.5 is 12 h 30 min) and it is stored as exact minutes. Required: use 0 if everything is billed by the hour.

overage_rate.what: What is charged for each hour worked beyond the cycle's available hours, in the contract's currency.
overage_rate.how: An amount with the same rules as the price: whole pesos in CLP, up to two decimals in UF. Required: use 0 if extra hours are not charged. The panel uses it to estimate what the cycle's overage costs.

rollover.what: Whether the hours not used in a cycle carry over to the next one.
rollover.how: Turn it on if the agreement lets hours accumulate. Two optional limits appear: how many hours can be carried and for how many cycles they last. Turning it off clears those limits on save.

rollover_max_hours.what: The cap on carried hours a cycle can bring from earlier ones.
rollover_max_hours.how: A number of hours, with decimals if you like. Empty means no cap.

rollover_max_cycles.what: How many cycles a carried hour survives before it expires.
rollover_max_cycles.how: A whole number between 1 and 120. Empty means they never expire.
rollover_max_cycles.example: 3 (March's hours can be used until June)

grace_days.what: How many days the covered apps keep working when the contract ends without being renewed.
grace_days.how: A whole number from 0 to {{max}}. During grace the apps warn that they are about to stop; when it ends, the service suspends them. With 0 they are suspended as soon as the contract ends.

grace_allows.what: What the apps may still do while in grace.
grace_allows.how: Tick what you want to keep: "Updates" lets them keep receiving new versions and "Support" lets them keep opening and continuing tickets. With nothing ticked, both stop during grace.

grace_message.what: The text the covered apps show while in grace.
grace_message.how: Write it for the people using the app, in their language, saying what is happening and whom to contact. Optional, up to 1000 characters.
grace_message.example: The maintenance contract has ended. The app will stop working on 10 March; contact your administrator.

notes.what: Internal notes about the contract: special terms, verbal agreements, context.
notes.how: Free text and optional, up to 5000 characters. Only shown in this panel; the client does not see it.
notes.example: Includes two on-site visits a year. Price frozen until 2027.

form_help.what: Defines what a client pays for: which apps it covers, for how long, what it costs, how many hours of work each cycle includes and what happens to the apps when it ends.
can_do: Pick the client and the covered apps.
Set the dates, automatic renewal and notice days.
Set the price and how often it is charged.
Define the hours per cycle, the overage rate and rollover.
Decide how many grace days the apps get and what they may do during them.
