form_help.on_save: Creating it takes you to the contract's page and the service starts keeping its hour cycles. Editing sends only what changed. Before the last day the service emails the client and the covered apps show the notice; if it ends without renewal, the apps go into grace or are suspended. Everything is written to the audit log. Once a cycle exists, the first day and the cycle length cannot be changed, and the client never can.

cycle.none: This contract has no running cycle.
cycle.overage_estimate: The overage would cost {{amount}} at {{rate}} per hour. It is an estimate while the cycle is open; closing it makes it final.
cycle.overage_no_rate: The contract has no overage rate, so the overage has no amount.
cycle.by_app_empty: No work logged in this cycle yet.
cycle.work_log_empty: No work was logged in this cycle.
cycle.history_description: Every cycle of the contract, newest first.
cycle.ended_open: Ended; closes on its own soon
cycle.close_body: The balance of the cycle {{range}} becomes final: unused hours carry over as the contract says, and no work can be logged or corrected in it any more. The service closes it on its own anyway.
cycle.bill_body: The cycle {{range}} is marked as billed.
cycle.bill_body_overage: The cycle {{range}} went {{time}} over, for {{amount}}. It is marked as billed.
cycle.reference_hint: The invoice or receipt number. Optional.

reference.what: The document the cycle was billed with, so it can be found later.
reference.how: Type the invoice or receipt number, with its type if that helps. Optional, up to 500 characters.

bill_form_help.what: Marks a closed cycle as billed, with the document's reference.
can_do: Note the invoice or receipt number.
bill_form_help.on_save: The cycle becomes "billed" and no longer counts in the overview as a cycle with overage to bill. Its balance was already final; this does not change it. It is written to the audit log.

work_log.title: Work log
work_log.description: The work done for the client, day by day.
work_log.description_contract: The work logged under this contract. It counts against the hours of the cycle each day falls in.
work_log.description_app: The work done on this app. Each entry counts against the contract covering it that day.
work_log.description_company: All the work done for this client, on its apps or in general.
work_log.delete_body: The work of {{day}} ({{time}}) will be deleted and its hours go back to the cycle.
work_log.locked: Its cycle is closed: the balance is final and the entry cannot change.
work_log.empty_description: Each entry carries the day, how long it took, what kind of work it was and what was done.
work_log.files_under: It will be filed under “{{name}}”, in the cycle that day falls in.
work_log.files_outside: No contract covers that day: it will be outside any contract.

hints.app: Empty when the work was for the client as a whole.
hints.link: A pull request, a ticket or a document. Optional.
hints.contract: More than one contract covers {{day}}: pick the one it is filed under.
hints.ticket: The support ticket this work answered. Optional.

errors.future: Work cannot be logged on a future day.
errors.outside_contract: That day is outside the contract's term.
errors.link: A full http or https address.
errors.choose_contract: More than one contract covers that day: pick one.
errors.closed_cycle: That day falls in a cycle that is already closed: its balance is final, and no work can be logged or changed in it.
errors.not_covered: That contract does not cover that day.
errors.ticket: That ticket belongs to another client: pick one of this client's, or none.

app.what: The app the work was about, if it was about one.
app.how: Pick the app, or "Client as a whole" if the work was for the client in general (a meeting, a report). It decides which contract it is filed under and which tickets can be chosen.

ticket.what: The support ticket this work answered.
ticket.how: Pick one of the app's tickets (or the client's, for general work). Optional. The service refuses another client's ticket. Linking it does not change which contract it is filed under: it only says what it answered.
ticket.example: #42 · The kiosk printer does not print receipts

kind.what: What kind of work it was.
kind.how: Maintenance for keeping what exists running, Support for helping users, Development for new features and Other for the rest. It is used for filtering and to see where the hours go.

description.what: What was done, for the client and for you a few months from now.
description.how: One or two concrete sentences. Required, up to 2000 characters.
description.example: Fixed the thermal printer driver and reinstalled the app on the entrance kiosk.

day.what: The day the work was done. It decides which contract and cycle the hours are counted against.
day.how: Pick today or an earlier day; future days are not accepted. From a contract's page it must fall within its term. A day inside an already closed cycle is refused, because its balance is final. Required.

duration.what: How long the work took, in hours and minutes.
duration.how: Type hours and minutes (0 to 59). Between 1 minute and {{max}} hours per entry; if it took longer, split it over several days. Required.

link.what: A link to what backs the work: a pull request, a ticket in the client's tracker, a document.
link.how: A full address starting with https:// or http://. Optional.

contract.what: Which contract the entry is filed under, when more than one covers that day.
contract.how: It only appears when several contracts cover the app (or the client) on that day; choosing one is then required. Normally the service picks it and the dialog says which.

form_help.what: Logs work done for a client, which is counted against its contract's hours.
can_do: Say which app and ticket it was about, what kind it was and what was done.
Note the day and how long it took.
Add a link that backs it.
Pick the contract if more than one covers that day.
form_help.on_save: The service files the entry under the contract covering the app (or the client) on that day and in the cycle the day falls in; the dialog says beforehand which it will be. The hours are counted against the cycle and show on the contract, the app, the client and the ticket. Editing sends only what changed. An entry in a closed cycle can no longer be changed. It is written to the audit log.

kind.what: Shows only the entries of one kind of work.
kind.how: Pick maintenance, support, development or other; "Every kind" removes the filter. The hours total follows the filter.

from.how: Pick a day; empty sets no earlier limit. It combines with "To".

to.how: Pick a day on or after "From"; empty sets no later limit.

ticket_statuses_hint.open: Waiting on us: new, or the requester wrote again.
ticket_statuses_hint.resolved: Done. If the requester writes again, it reopens.
ticket_statuses_hint.closed: Done for good: the requester has to open a new one.

tickets.title: Support tickets
tickets.description: What people ask for from inside the clients' apps. Refreshes every 30 seconds.
tickets.empty_description: When somebody opens a ticket from an app with the support module, it shows up here.
tickets.subject: Subject
tickets.conversation_description: What the requester wrote from the app and what they were told. The app reads answers the next time it asks for the ticket.
tickets.reply_hint: The app shows it the next time it asks for the ticket. No email is sent.
tickets.closed_notice: This ticket is closed: the requester can no longer write on it. Change its status to reopen it.
tickets.context_description: What the device looked like when the ticket was opened. Kept with the ticket; it never changes.
tickets.open_diagnostics: See the app's crashes and logs
tickets.no_diagnostics: No diagnostics attached: the app has neither the logs nor the crashes module, or the requester did not send them.
tickets.no_context: This ticket carries no device context.
tickets.work_log_description: The work done to answer this ticket. It counts against the contract covering the app on that day, like any other work log entry.

installation_panel.title: Support tickets
installation_panel.description: Tickets opened from this device, newest first.
installation_panel.empty: This device has opened no tickets
installation_panel.empty_description: When somebody opens a ticket from the app on this device, it shows up here.

assignee.title: Support
assignee.description: Who hears in the site's bell about every new ticket of this app and every message the requester adds. No email is sent.
assignee.taken: You now receive this app's tickets.
assignee.yours: You already receive this app's tickets.

tickets.hint_one: {{count}} ticket is waiting for an answer
tickets.hint_other: {{count}} tickets are waiting for an answer

status.what: The ticket's status, which says whose turn it is.
status.how: Open waits for our answer; Pending was answered and waits on the requester; Resolved is done but reopens if the requester writes again; Closed is done for good. Changing it here writes to nobody; to reopen one, choose Open.
status.example: Resolved, once the requester confirmed it works

reply.what: The answer to the requester, which the app shows inside its support screen.
reply.how: Write in the requester's language and explain what was done or what you need from them. Required to send, up to 5000 characters. No email is sent: the app shows it the next time it fetches the ticket.
reply.example: Hi Carolina, we fixed the printing error. Restart the kiosk and let us know if it happens again.

status_after.what: Which status the ticket is left in after sending the answer.
status_after.how: Pending (the default) when you expect the requester to reply; Resolved when the answer solves it; Closed when there is nothing more to do and it must not reopen.

subject.what: The ticket's subject: what it is about, in one line.
subject.how: Correct it so it reads well in the inbox. Required, up to 200 characters. The client's app also sees it when listing its tickets.
subject.example: The kiosk printer does not print receipts

form_help.what: Answers the ticket's requester from the panel; the client's app shows the answer in its support screen.
can_do: Write the answer.
Choose which status the ticket is left in afterwards.
form_help.on_save: The answer is added to the conversation, which shows whether the app has read it yet. No email is sent. The ticket is left in the chosen status (Pending by default). It is written to the audit log. To log the time it took, use "Log work" in the ticket's time panel.

can_do: Rewrite the subject so it reads well in the inbox.
subject_form_help.on_save: The new subject shows in the panel and in the client's app. The requester is not notified. It is written to the audit log.

search.what: Searches tickets by their text or number.
search.how: Type part of the subject or of the requester's name or email, or "#" and the number to go to one. The service does the matching.

status.what: Shows the tickets in one status.
status.how: "Needs attention" (the default) combines Open and Pending; you can also pick one status or "Every status". It is kept in the address.

app.what: Shows only the tickets opened from one app.
app.how: Pick the app; "Every app" removes the filter. It is kept in the address.

company.how: Pick the client; "Every client" removes the filter. It is kept in the address.
